prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone in St. Louis — the right choice depends on your project (whole house vs one room, residential vs commercial), budget, schedule, and how much prep/repair work you need. I can help you pick the best one for your needs. To get you started, here’s a practical guide for finding and vetting the top interior painters in St. Louis.

What to look for
- Positive recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi/Angie’s List and/or the BBB (look for patterns, not single comments).
- Proper insurance (general liability and workers’ comp) and business license.
- Portfolio of recent interior work and references from local customers.
- Clear, itemized written estimate (labor, paint brand/finish, number of coats, prep, cleanup).
- Good communication and responsiveness.
- Warranty or guarantee on workmanship and paint.
- Experience with the surface types you have (plaster, drywall, trim, cabinets).

Step-by-step hiring process
1. Get at least 3 written estimates from different companies.
2. Confirm each company’s insurance and licensing; ask for certificates.
3. Ask for 2–3 local references and pictures of finished jobs.
4. Verify which paint brands and number of coats are included.
5. Have a written contract with start/end dates, payment schedule, scope, and cleanup terms.
6. Keep the final payment until you’re satisfied with the job and punch-list items are completed.

Important questions to ask a painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
- Who will do the work — your employees or subcontractors?
- Which paint brands and finishes do you use (and why)?
- How many coats and what kind of primer will you apply?
- How will you protect floors/furniture and handle cleanup?
- Do you provide a written warranty? What does it cover and for how long?
- What is the payment schedule and do you require deposits?

Red flags
- No written estimate or contract.
- Poor or no proof of insurance.
- Extremely low bids (often cut corners).
- Pressure to pay large sums upfront.
- Consistent negative reviews citing the same issues.

Typical price ranges (ballpark)
- Single small room (one coat touch-up): $150–$400
- Standard 12x12 room (walls only, 2 coats): $300–$900
- Whole house interior (per room varies): $300–$1,200 per room depending on prep, trim, ceilings
Prices depend on condition, ceiling height, trim complexity, paint quality, and prep/repairs.

How I can help next
- If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you want a franchise or a local shop, I can:
  - Draft a short request-for-quote message/email to send to painters.
  - Provide a checklist you can take on site when they give estimates.
  - Outline what to include in the contract/punch list.

Would you like me to draft an email/phone script and a shortlist checklist? If so, give me your ZIP code and any preferences (budget, timeline, whole house vs specific rooms).
